items.title: Accidental Payment Scam: Don't Send Money Back
items.summary:
You get an unexpected payment — Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, or a text
message says someone sent you money by mistake. Then a message follows:
"They accidentally sent you money, please send it back." If you send it
back, you lose. The original payment may be fraudulent and get reversed
by the bank, but the money you voluntarily sent is gone for good.

What to do: Do not send money back. Leave the funds untouched and
contact your bank or payment service through its official app, website,
or customer-service number. Do not trust screenshots or messages from
the sender as proof. Avoid clicking links from strangers — they lead to
fake login pages.

This matters: Scammers use stolen cards or hacked accounts to send the

items.title: AI Voice Clone Scams Are Calling — Hang Up and Call Back on a Known Number
items.summary:
AI voice clone scams are calling people right now. The caller sounds exactly like a family member — a grandchild, a child, a spouse — and says they're in trouble. They need money immediately for bail, a car repair, a medical emergency. It's not them. Scammers use AI to clone voices from social media videos.

The call feels real because the voice is real — it's a copy of someone you love. The scammer pressures you to act fast, send money, don't tell anyone.

What to do: Hang up. Call the person back on a number you know is theirs. If you can't reach them, call another family member to check. Never send money or gift cards based on a surprise call, no matter how real the voice sounds.
